key_responsibilities: Design, develop, test C++ trading applications
Translate trader requirements into technical solutions
Full lifecycle from idea to production support

strengths: Performance tuning is real depth: CUDA kernel work took VGG16 from 73.3 ms to 49.2 ms, TensorRT YOLO got 5.2x (56.7 to 10.9 ms), and the MPI ray tracer reached 30x with measured load-imbalance analysis
Real-time and concurrency-adjacent: STM32 bare-metal ISR/timer firmware at deterministic 1 Hz in 3.68 KB Flash, FreeRTOS with mutexes on the turret, multiprocessing capture pipeline in COFFIN
Profiling and troubleshooting habit: pynvml VRAM/latency profiling on TinyLlama; resolved 11 integration failures to reach 10/10 pick reliability
real_gaps: No data structures and algorithms evidence anywhere in the profile
C++ is shown only as CUDA kernels and Arduino IK; no C++ application with class design, STL, or C++17/20 features
Threading is RTOS mutexes and MPI processes; no std::thread, atomics, lock-free or contention work
No finance, market data, order book or low-latency network work
All production-style work is capstone/research/internship scope
overstated_by_keywords: object-oriented design counted Adjacent, but the modular Frame Simulator is Python and the C++ work is procedural kernels
C++17/20 counted Adjacent to C++, but there is no modern-C++ evidence
understated_by_keywords: MPI scaling studies and CUDA memory coalescing show genuine performance-engineering reasoning that maps to latency-sensitive trading code
Bare-metal ISR and timer work is real determinism experience
screening_gaps: No demonstrable data structures and algorithms strength, which prop-firm C++ screens (coding rounds) lean on hardest
No C++ application-level evidence (OOD, STL, C++17/20, std::thread/atomics); C++ appears only in CUDA and Arduino contexts
No finance or low-latency trading-systems exposure to show the interest the JD asks for
llm_analysis.reasoning: The role is entry level and rewards performance tuning, real-time thinking and measurement, which are your strongest genuine areas. The risk is the screen itself: a trading firm will test DSA and C++ fluency directly, and the profile has no evidence for either beyond kernels and firmware. Worth applying, but only if you are ready for a C++/DSA coding round.

outcome.notes: Rejected after completing the online assessment; moved forward with other candidates. No feedback.
